chapter: Small band, Charlie Parker and the big band
title: How long Bird stayed with the big band
summary: McShann dates Bird's stay with the big band to about four years, from 1940 to late 1943, after which Bird lost interest.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: Listen, Jay, how long was Bird with you in the big band? How long a period was that?
Bird was with the big band from the time he joined Harlan Leonard --
That's after he left Harlan and came with you, huh?
He stayed with the big band until -- I think I let Bird go in Detroit and that was 1940 -- about the last of '43, pert-near '44.
So how long would that have been? About --
So that had to be -- '40, '41, '42, '43, four years.
No kidding? No wonder you say he was blowing his best stuff then.
That's right. That was four years. See, and --
He really found himself in a big band right there.
That's right. And then the thing

about it, see, when Bird started getting into this other thing we was talking about, started getting into that, all he wanted to do was put his horn on his arm and just go down to Monroe's, Minton's, and just like I go in there and get me a taste, little couple of tunes, get off, come back in another hour and get a couple of tastes, go blow a tune. He didn't have his heart like it was with that big band.
